content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 11
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
29 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 1
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Solomon loved many foreign women — and-the-daughter-of Pharaoh — Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and-Hittite —

**LOGOS (formal):** Now King Solomon loved many foreign women, along with the daughter of Pharaoh: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** King Solomon loved many foreign women besides Pharaoh's daughter — women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the Hittites.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 2
**EMET (literal):** from the-nations of-which YHWH said to the-sons-of Israel, "You-shall-not go among-them and-they shall-not go among-you; surely they-will-turn ʾet-your-heart after their-gods." To-them Solomon clung in-love.

**LOGOS (formal):** from the nations concerning which the LORD had said to the people of Israel, "You shall not enter into marriage with them, neither shall they with you, for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods." Solomon clung to these in love.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** They came from the very nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, "You must not intermarry with them, because they will surely turn your hearts to their gods." Yet Solomon held fast to them in love.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-he-had wives — princesses: seven hundred; and-concubines: three hundred. And-his-wives turned ʾet-his-heart.

**LOGOS (formal):** He had seven hundred wives, who were princesses, and three hundred concubines. And his wives turned away his heart.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines — and his wives led his heart astray.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was at-the-time-of the-old-age-of Solomon, his-wives turned ʾet-his-heart after other gods, and-his-heart was-not complete with YHWH his-God, as the-heart-of David his-father.

**LOGOS (formal):** For when Solomon was old his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** As Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart toward other gods. His heart was no longer fully devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David's heart had been.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the-goddess-of the-Sidonians, and-after Milcom, the-abomination-of the-Ammonites.

**LOGOS (formal):** For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the detestable god of the Ammonites.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-so he-did for-all his-foreign wives, who-burned-incense and-sacrificed to-their-gods.

**LOGOS (formal):** And so he did for all his foreign wives, who made offerings and sacrificed to their gods.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** and-had-commanded-him concerning this thing, not to-go after other gods. But-he-did-not keep ʾet-what YHWH commanded.

**LOGOS (formal):** and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods. But he did not keep what the LORD commanded.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** and had specifically warned him about this very thing — not to follow other gods. But Solomon refused to obey.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** for six months Joab dwelt there, and-all Israel, until he-had-cut-off every male in-Edom —

**LOGOS (formal):** For six months Joab and all Israel remained there, until he had cut off every male in Edom.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Joab and all the Israelites stayed there six months, until they had killed every male.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** and-Hadad fled, he and-certain Edomite men from-the-servants-of his-father with-him, to-go to-Egypt. And-Hadad was a-small youth.

**LOGOS (formal):** But Hadad fled to Egypt, together with certain Edomites of his father's servants, Hadad being yet a little child.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But Hadad, still a young boy, escaped to Egypt with some of his father's Edomite officials.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-they-arose from-Midian and-came to-Paran, and-they-took men with-them from-Paran and-came to-Egypt, to-Pharaoh king-of Egypt, and-he-gave to-him a-house and-food he-assigned to-him and-land he-gave to-him.

**LOGOS (formal):** They set out from Midian and came to Paran and took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house and assigned him an allowance of food and gave him land.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** They left Midian, traveled through Paran, picked up more men along the way, and arrived in Egypt. Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, a food allowance, and land.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 19
**EMET (literal):** And-Hadad found great favor in-the-eyes-of Pharaoh, and-he-gave to-him a-wife — the-sister-of his-own-wife, the-sister-of Tahpenes the-queen.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him in marriage the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Hadad gained such favor with Pharaoh that the king gave him his wife's sister — Queen Tahpenes's sister — in marriage.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 20
**EMET (literal):** And-the-sister-of Tahpenes bore to-him ʾet-Genubath his-son, and-Tahpenes weaned-him in-the-midst-of the-house-of Pharaoh. And-Genubath was in-the-house-of Pharaoh among the-sons-of Pharaoh.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house. And Genubath was in Pharaoh's house among the sons of Pharaoh.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Tahpenes's sister bore him a son, Genubath, whom Tahpenes raised in the palace alongside Pharaoh's own children.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 22
**EMET (literal):** And-Pharaoh said to-him, "But what are-you lacking with-me, that behold, you are-seeking to-go to your-land?" And-he-said, "Nothing, but sending you-must-send-me."

**LOGOS (formal):** But Pharaoh said to him, "What have you lacked with me that you are now seeking to go to your own country?" And he said to him, "Only let me go."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "What have you lacked here that makes you want to leave?" Pharaoh asked. "Nothing," Hadad replied, "but please let me go."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 23
**EMET (literal):** And-God raised-up to-him an-adversary — Rezon son-of Eliada, who had-fled from Hadadezer king-of Zobah, his-master.

**LOGOS (formal):** God also raised up as an adversary to him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** God also raised up another adversary against Solomon — Rezon son of Eliada, who had deserted his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** And-he-gathered to-himself men and-became commander-of a-raiding-band when-David killed-them. And-they-went to-Damascus and-dwelt in-it and-reigned in-Damascus.

**LOGOS (formal):** And he gathered men about him and became leader of a marauding band, after the killing by David. And they went to Damascus and lived there and made him king in Damascus.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** After David's victories, Rezon gathered a band of rebels and went to Damascus, where they settled and he became king.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** And-he-was an-adversary to-Israel all the-days-of Solomon — and-the-evil that Hadad did — and-he-loathed Israel and-reigned over Aram.

**LOGOS (formal):** He was an adversary of Israel all the days of Solomon, doing harm as Hadad did. And he loathed Israel and reigned over Syria.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Rezon was hostile to Israel throughout Solomon's reign, compounding the trouble caused by Hadad. He ruled over Aram and was a constant threat to Israel.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** And-this is the-matter why he-raised a-hand against the-king: Solomon built ʾet-the-Millo; he-closed ʾet-the-breach-of the-City-of David his-father.

**LOGOS (formal):** And this was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon built the Millo and closed up the breach of the city of David his father.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** This is the story of his rebellion: Solomon was building the Millo, closing the gap in the wall of the City of David.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 28
**EMET (literal):** And-the-man Jeroboam was a-mighty-man-of valor. And-Solomon saw the-young-man that he was doing work, and-he-appointed-him over all the-forced-labor-of the-house-of Joseph.

**LOGOS (formal):** The man Jeroboam was very able, and when Solomon saw that the young man was industrious, he gave him charge over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Jeroboam was an exceptionally capable man. When Solomon noticed how industrious this young man was, he put him in charge of the entire labor force of the tribes of Joseph.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 29
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was at-that time, and-Jeroboam went-out from-Jerusalem, and-Ahijah the-Shilonite, the-prophet, found-him on-the-way, and-he was-clothed with-a-new garment. And-the-two-of-them were alone in-the-field.

**LOGOS (formal):** And at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Now Ahijah had dressed himself in a new garment, and the two of them were alone in the open country.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** One day, as Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah of Shiloh met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the countryside.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 30
**EMET (literal):** And-Ahijah seized the-new garment that was upon-him, and-tore-it — twelve pieces.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then Ahijah laid hold of the new garment that was on him, and tore it into twelve pieces.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Ahijah grabbed the new cloak he was wearing and ripped it into twelve pieces.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 33
**EMET (literal):** Because they-forsook-me and-bowed-down to-Ashtoreth goddess-of the-Sidonians, to-Chemosh god-of Moab, and-to-Milcom god-of the-sons-of Ammon, and-did-not walk in-my-ways, to-do the-right in-my-eyes and-my-statutes and-my-judgments, as David his-father.

**LOGOS (formal):** because they have forsaken me and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites, and they have not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my sight and keeping my statutes and my rules, as David his father did.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** I am doing this because they have abandoned me and worshiped Ashtoreth goddess of Sidon, Chemosh god of Moab, and Milcom god of Ammon. They have not walked in my ways or done what is right in my eyes or kept my laws and regulations as David, Solomon's father, did.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 34
**EMET (literal):** And-I-will-not take ʾet-all the-kingdom from-his-hand, for prince I-will-set-him all the-days-of his-life, for-the-sake-of David my-servant whom I-chose, who kept my-commandments and-my-statutes.

**LOGOS (formal):** Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But I will not take the whole kingdom from Solomon. I will let him be ruler for the rest of his life, for the sake of my servant David, whom I chose because he obeyed my commands and decrees.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 35
**EMET (literal):** And-I-will-take the-kingdom from-the-hand-of his-son, and-give-it to-you — ʾet-the-ten tribes.

**LOGOS (formal):** But I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand and will give it to you, ten tribes.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** I will take the kingdom from his son and give you ten tribes.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 37
**EMET (literal):** And-you I-will-take, and-you-will-reign over all that your-soul desires, and-you-will-be king over Israel.

**LOGOS (formal):** And I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** As for you, I will take you, and you will rule over everything your heart desires. You will be king over Israel.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 39
**EMET (literal):** And-I-will-afflict ʾet-the-seed-of David because-of this — only not all the-days.'"

**LOGOS (formal):** And I will afflict the offspring of David because of this, but not forever.'"

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** I will humble David's descendants because of this — but not forever.'"

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 40
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon sought to-kill ʾet-Jeroboam. And-Jeroboam arose and-fled to-Egypt, to Shishak king-of Egypt, and-he-was in-Egypt until the-death-of Solomon.

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled into Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Egypt, to King Shishak, and stayed there until Solomon died.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 41
**EMET (literal):** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Solomon, and-all that he-did, and-his-wisdom — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Acts-of Solomon?

**LOGOS (formal):** Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** As for the rest of Solomon's reign — everything he did and the wisdom he showed — it is all recorded in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 42
**EMET (literal):** And-the-days that Solomon reigned in-Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 43
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon lay-down with his-fathers, and-was-buried in-the-City-of David his-father. And-Rehoboam his-son reigned in-his-place.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father. And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then Solomon died and was buried in the City of David. His son Rehoboam succeeded him as king.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
